PART I

Item 1. Business

BUSINESS-BODY-MARKER. Example Semiconductor Corp designs analog and mixed-signal chips for automotive and industrial customers. We rely on third-party foundries, primarily Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, to fabricate our wafers, and on outsourced assembly and test providers such as Amkor Technology to package them.

Our largest customers include tier-one automotive suppliers and global distributors. One distributor accounted for 14% of net revenue in fiscal 2025. We compete with Texas Instruments, Analog Devices and Microchip Technology. See Item 1A for risks related to our dependence on these suppliers.

We had approximately 4,200 employees at fiscal year end, of whom about half work in research and development.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

RISK-BODY-MARKER. Investing in our common stock involves risk. You should carefully consider the risks described below together with the other information in this report.

We depend on a limited number of third-party foundries. Substantially all of our wafers are manufactured by TSMC. Any disruption at its facilities in Taiwan, including from earthquakes, power shortages or geopolitical tension, could delay shipments and materially harm our results.

Export controls could limit our sales. New restrictions on shipments to China could reduce demand for our products and require us to obtain licenses we may not receive.

Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments

None.

Item 1C. Cybersecurity

CYBER-BODY-MARKER. Our board's audit committee oversees our cybersecurity risk management program, which is led by our Chief Information Security Officer.

Item 2. Properties

Our headquarters are located in San Jose, California.
